name: Sikorsky S-58 / H-34
summary: A Korean War-era transport with the radial engine in the nose and cockpit above it; flown by firefighters and collectors today.

wings: Four-blade main rotor on a tall mast
engines: Radial piston engine in the nose behind clamshell doors
S-58T turbine conversion has a Twin-Pac in the nose behind a cowling with twin rectangular intakes
fuselage: Large round nose with the cockpit perched above the engine
tail: Tail rotor and a stabilizer on the side

tellTales: Engine in the nose with the cockpit perched above it
Four-blade rotor over a boxy fuselage
Tailwheel gear with a canted tail pylon

confusedWith.howToTell: The S-55 has three blades and a smaller body; the S-58 has four blades and is larger and boxier.
The S-61 has turbines on the roof and a boat hull; the S-58 has a nose engine and a smaller body.
The Huey has a turbine on top and a slim nose with a two-blade rotor; the S-58 has four blades and a bulbous nose.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
